accepted.x: Only about 5% of marriages are estimated to be inter-caste.

accepted.s: The Dr Ambedkar Scheme provides what amount to inter-caste couples?
accepted.x: The Dr Ambedkar Scheme provides ₹2.5 lakh to inter-caste couples.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact benefit amount from nearby plausible figures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Honour killings tend to rise when caste hierarchy is challenged.
2. Inter-caste marriages constitute the majority of marriages in India.
3. The Dr Ambedkar Scheme provides financial assistance to inter-caste couples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because only about 5% of marriages are inter-caste.
accepted.tq: Identify the extreme and reversed-share statement before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

accepted.s: The Supreme Court protected live-in relationships under which Article of the Constitution?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court recognised protection for live-in relationships under Article 21 in 2010.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional protection with the precise Article number.
accepted.sec: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code is correct?
o: It makes registration of live-in relationships mandatory.
It recognises only religious marriages and excludes civil marriages.
It applies only to inter-caste couples.
accepted.x: Uttarakhand's UCC makes registration of live-in relationships mandatory.
accepted.tq: Apply the specific legal requirement to the live-in relationship scenario.
accepted.sec: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

accepted.s:
With reference to the Supreme Court's decisions on same-sex relationships and marriage, consider the following statements:
1. Navtej Singh Johar (2018) read down Section 377.
2. In Supriyo, the Supreme Court read same-sex marriage into the Special Marriage Act.
3. Chief Justice Chandrachud was in the minority in Supriyo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Supriyo, decided in October 2023, refused to read same-sex marriage into the Special Marriage Act.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed outcome in the second statement while retaining the correct date-linked holdings.
accepted.sec: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a contemporary trend in marriage?
accepted.x: Companionate marriage, rising age at marriage, serial monogamy and increasing divorce are identified trends. Universal return to child marriage is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of the stated social trends.
accepted.sec: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

accepted.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum marriageable age is:
o: 21 years for both women and men
18 years for both women and men
18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
accepted.x: The PCMA, 2006 prescribes 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two age thresholds instead of treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: A marriage involving a child under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, is generally:
o: Void only when solemnised by a priest
Voidable at the option of the child
accepted.x: Under the PCMA, the marriage is voidable at the option of the child; it is not automatically void in every case.
accepted.tq: Distinguish voidable from automatically void, a common legal-status trap.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s:
The PCM (Amendment) Bill, 2025 proposed which combination of measures?
1. Raising the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years.
2. Creating a Central Reporting Portal.
3. Reducing the minimum marriageable age of men to 18 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill proposed raising women's minimum age to 21 and creating a Central Reporting Portal. It did not propose reducing men's age to 18.
accepted.tq: Separate the proposed amendments from the unchanged male age threshold.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: The Allahabad High Court held in July 2026 that the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act:
o: Overrides the personal-law puberty rule for all religions
Applies only where both parties are below 18
Does not apply to marriages governed by personal law
accepted.x: On 1 July 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA overrides the personal-law puberty rule for all religions.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of the ruling and avoid the personal-law exception trap.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: According to NFHS-6, what percentage of women aged 20–24 were married before attaining 18 years?
accepted.x: NFHS-6 reported that 20.1% of women aged 20–24 were married before 18; the rural figure was 23.3%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall NFHS-6 figure from the rural and earlier-survey figures.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s:
Arrange the following figures in chronological order according to the NFHS survey series:
A. 20.1%
B. 26.8%
C. 23.3%
Which of the following is the correct sequence?
accepted.x: The figures were 26.8% in NFHS-4, 23.3% in NFHS-5 and 20.1% in NFHS-6.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence to NFHS-4, NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 before comparing the percentages.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: Which organisation's publication records cases registered under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act?
accepted.x: The National Crime Records Bureau records PCMA cases in its Crime in India publication.
accepted.tq: Match the offence data source with the responsible statistical body.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat initiative aims to:
o: Reduce child marriage by 50% by 2025 and eliminate it by 2028
Register all marriages by 2030 without setting a reduction target
Reduce child marriage by 10% by 2026 and eliminate it by 2030
Eliminate child marriage by 2026 and reduce it by 10% by 2030
accepted.x: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat aims to cut child marriage by 10% by 2026 and eliminate it by 2030.
accepted.tq: Keep the reduction target and elimination target in their correct years.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: A 100-day drive under Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat commenced in:
accepted.x: The 100-day drive commenced in December 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch month from the target years of the wider initiative.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: ALIVA, a data-driven approach to addressing child marriage, originated in which district?
accepted.x: ALIVA is a data-driven approach from Nayagarh district of Odisha.
accepted.tq: Check both the district and the State rather than relying on the district name alone.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the legislative history of the Sarda Act?
o: Enacted in 1929, came into force in 1930 and amended in 1978
Enacted in 1930, came into force in 1931 and amended in 1978
Enacted in 1929, came into force in 1930 and repealed in 1978
Enacted in 1978, came into force in 1979 and amended in 1929
accepted.x: The Sarda Act was enacted in 1929, came into force in 1930 and was amended in 1978.
accepted.tq: Separate enactment, commencement and amendment years in the correct order.
accepted.sec: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

accepted.s: The provisions relating to marriage offences in IPC Chapter XX, Sections 493–498, were reorganised under which provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
accepted.x: IPC Chapter XX, Sections 493–498, became BNS Sections 81–84 in the stated reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Avoid the nearby-section trap by pairing the old chapter with its new range.
accepted.sec: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

accepted.s: Bigamy is dealt with under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in the stated framework?
accepted.x: Bigamy is placed under BNS Section 82, corresponding to old IPC Sections 494–495.
accepted.tq: Use the old-to-new section correspondence to separate bigamy from adjacent marriage offences.
accepted.sec: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill, 2025:
1. It makes polygamy a cognizable offence.
2. It makes the offence non-bailable.
3. It provides for imprisonment up to seven years' rigorous imprisonment.
4. Sixth Schedule areas are exempt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the Bill makes polygamy cognizable and non-bailable, provides up to seven years' rigorous imprisonment, and exempts Sixth Schedule areas.
accepted.tq: Verify each legal consequence and the territorial exception before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

accepted.s: Self-respect marriages were institutionalised by Periyar and validated in Tamil Nadu through which provision?
o: Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act
Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act
Section 8 of the Hindu Marriage Act
Section 5 of the Special Marriage Act
accepted.x: Self-respect marriages were institutionalised by Periyar and validated through Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act by a Tamil Nadu amendment in 1967.
accepted.tq: Match the social reform movement with its specific statutory provision.
accepted.sec: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Satyashodhak marriage tradition?
o: It required a Brahmin priest and dowry payment.
It was a form of marriage exclusively involving several men and several women.
It used no dowry and no Brahmin priest.
It could be solemnised only by a Marriage Officer under the SMA.
accepted.x: Satyashodhak marriage, started by Savitribai Phule, used no dowry and no Brahmin priest.
accepted.tq: Reject the options that import features of other marriage forms or solemnisation systems.
accepted.sec: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

accepted.s: Monogamy may be classified into:
accepted.x: Monogamy is classified as serial or non-serial monogamy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the classification of monogamy from classifications used for polygyny and polyandry.

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Fraternal polyandry — Khas
2. Sororal polygyny — marriage involving sisters
3. Group marriage — several men with several women
4. Polygyny — permitted for Muslims
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Fraternal polyandry is associated with the Khas, sororal polygyny concerns sisters, group marriage involves several men and women, and polygyny is permitted for Muslims.
accepted.tq: Check the defining feature of each marriage form rather than treating the terms as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s:
Fraternal polyandry is associated with which of the following groups or regions?
1. Khas of Uttarakhand
2. Ladakh
3. Toda
4. Nayagarh
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Fraternal polyandry is associated with the Khas of Uttarakhand, Ladakh and the Toda. Nayagarh is associated with the ALIVA child-marriage initiative, not polyandry.
accepted.tq: Separate the marriage anthropology examples from the district associated with a child-marriage programme.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s: Group marriage refers to a form in which:
o: One woman marries several brothers only.
One man marries one woman successively at different times.
Several men are married to several women as a group.
A bride is given to a Veda-learned groom.
accepted.x: Group marriage involves several men with several women.
accepted.tq: Use the number and gender combination in the definition to distinguish group marriage from polyandry and monogamy.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a form of marriage described in Manu's classification?
o: Brahma — marriage to a Veda-learned groom
Arsha — exchange involving a cow and a bull, not a sale
Prajapatya — marriage based on bride price
accepted.x: Prajapatya involves joint dharma. Bride price is associated with the Asura form; Arsha involves a cow and bull and is not treated as a sale.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped defining feature among closely related classifications.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the eight forms of marriage:
1. Gandharva is based on mutual consent.
2. Rakshasa involves force.
3. Paishacha is regarded as the lowest form.
4. Asura involves bride price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Gandharva is based on mutual consent, Rakshasa on force, Paishacha is the lowest form, and Asura involves bride price.
accepted.tq: Test each form by its defining element and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s: How many forms of marriage are recognised in both Manu's classification and Kautilya's classification?
accepted.x: Both Manu and Kautilya describe eight forms of marriage.
accepted.tq: Retain the common count and avoid confusing it with the four approved forms.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the classification of marriage forms is correct?
o: All eight forms are listed as approved forms.
Only Manu, and not Kautilya, recognised eight forms.
Brahma, Daiva, Arsha and Prajapatya are the four approved forms listed here.
Gandharva, Rakshasa and Paishacha are the three approved forms.
accepted.x: The four approved forms listed are Brahma, Daiva, Arsha and Prajapatya. Manu and Kautilya both recognised eight forms, while the remaining four listed forms are unapproved.
accepted.tq: Compare the approved subset with the complete eight-form classification.
accepted.sec: Forms of marriage - monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, group marriage, Manu's forms

accepted.s: Amit Shah stated that the Uniform Civil Code would cover all 21 NDA-ruled States by which year?
accepted.x: The stated target is to cover all 21 NDA States by 2029.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the UCC expansion target year from the child-marriage elimination year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the current status of the Uniform Civil Code measures mentioned?
o: Uttarakhand's UCC has been in force since January 2024, while all three other Bills have received assent.
Uttarakhand's UCC has been in force since January 2025, while the Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh Bills await Presidential assent.
The Uttarakhand UCC has not yet been enacted and all four measures are pending.
Only Assam's Bill awaits assent; Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh have no UCC Bills.
accepted.x: Uttarakhand's UCC has been in force since January 2025. The UCC Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were stated to be awaiting Presidential assent.
accepted.tq: Separate an enacted State measure from Bills awaiting Presidential assent.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: What was the conclusion of the 21st Law Commission in 2018 regarding a Uniform Civil Code?
o: It was neither necessary nor desirable at that stage.
It had already replaced all personal laws.
It was desirable only for tribal areas.
It was constitutionally mandatory and immediately necessary.
accepted.x: The 21st Law Commission in 2018 found a Uniform Civil Code to be neither necessary nor desirable.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Commission's evaluative conclusion from constitutional or legislative outcomes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: An adolescent-education programme in Andhra Pradesh covering child marriage operates in how many schools?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh adolescent-education programme covers child marriage in 9,675 schools.
